solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bars to limit stock

parts.note: surface reading: rules capping how much a shop or investor may hold
setter's reading: metal bars set in a road that farm animals will not walk across

explanation.surface: A regulator imposes caps on how much stock can be held.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' sounds financial, and 'bars' like prohibitions; read literally they are livestock and metal rails.
explanation.definitionFit: A cattle grid is a set of spaced rails over a pit in a road that livestock refuse to cross, so it keeps them confined.

clue.text: Judge gets a lift carrying pages

indicators.note: something carrying another holds it within itself

parts.note: taken as written
pp. is the abbreviation for pages
to lift is to raise

explanation.surface: A judge takes the lift up, holding some documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrying' tells you the lift holds the pages inside it, after the opening A.
explanation.definitionFit: To appraise is to assess the value or quality of something, which is to judge it.

clue.text: Regularly get into western garb

definitions.note: a tie is one item of garb rather than garb as a whole

indicators.note: going west means travelling right to left, the reverse of normal reading
regularly means taking letters at even intervals, every other one

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters of get into

explanation.surface: Someone routinely dresses up in cowboy clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Western' is a reversal signal meant for across clues; in a down clue it still means reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie is a neckwear item, part of what one wears, so loosely an item of garb.

clue.text: Does it grow down as it grows up?

definitions.text: Does it grow down as it grows up?

parts.words: Does it grow down as it grows up?
parts.note: surface reading: a riddle about something that shrinks as it gets older

parts.words: Does it grow down as it grows up?
parts.note: setter's reading: a sea duck famous for soft feathers it develops as it matures

explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' looks like a direction opposed to 'up', but it is soft fluffy feather, as in the quilt named after this bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The eider is a large sea duck whose fine breast feathers are gathered to fill quilts known as eiderdowns.

clue.text: The German overturning binding European regulations

definitions.note: red tape is any bureaucratic regulation; European adds the stereotype of Brussels rules

indicators.note: overturned in a down clue means turned upside down, so read from the bottom

parts.note: der is a German word for 'the'
tape is used for binding

explanation.surface: A German official protests by flouting EU rules that bind him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European' does no work in the wordplay; it only colours the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Red tape is excessive bureaucratic procedure, named after the ribbon once used to tie official documents.

clue.text: Daughter, scruffy and boozing, continued tediously

parts.note: standard abbreviation
ragged clothes are scruffy
someone on the bottle or on a bender is boozing

explanation.surface: A dishevelled, drinking daughter rambled on endlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that dragged on lasted far too long and became boring.

clue.text: Drop a heroic tale

parts.note: to sag is to droop or drop
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is told to abandon an epic story.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long Norse or Icelandic narrative of heroic deeds, hence any heroic tale.

clue.text: Toy helmets scattered round a big house

indicators.note: scattered items are strewn about out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; 'round' places it among the jumbled letters

explanation.surface: Children's play helmets are strewn about a mansion.
explanation.definitionFit: A stately home is a large grand country house, often owned by aristocrats and open to the public.

clue.text: Rubbish in front of cave

parts.note: grot is British slang for junk or filth
'to' means before, as in ten to six

explanation.surface: Litter has piled up at the mouth of a cave.
explanation.walkthrough: TO for 'in front of' is a stretch, from telling the time.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotto is a small picturesque cave, natural or artificial.

clue.text: Brilliant Spanish tennis ace cut off pass

indicators.note: something cut off loses its end, so the player's surname drops its final letter

parts.note: Sp. is the standard abbreviation for Spanish
Ivan Lendl, former world number one tennis player
an ID card serves as a pass

explanation.surface: A star Spanish tennis player is somehow cut off from a mountain pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spanish tennis ace' suggests Nadal, but Spanish is only SP; the ace is Ivan Lendl, a Czech-born player.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendid and brilliant are synonyms, both meaning excellent or magnificent.

clue.text: Flower a maiden attached to a short belt

indicators.note: short means the word is curtailed, losing its last letter

parts.note: taken as written
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over
taken as written
a belt is a zone, as in a commuter belt

explanation.surface: A girl's dress fastened with a little belt, decorated with a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is crossword code for something that flows: a river, here the great South American one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amazon is a river, and a river is a 'flower' in the crossword sense of something that flows.

clue.text: A shrew damaged heavy rope

indicators.note: damaged things are knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A small rodent has gnawed through a thick rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A hawser is a thick cable used for mooring or towing a ship.

clue.text: Way cyborg crime fighter arrests small Egyptian flasher?

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: a police officer who arrests someone holds them in custody, wrapped up

parts.note: RoboCop is the cyborg police officer in the 1987 film
standard clothing-size abbreviation
E is used for Egyptian, as in the Egyptian pound

explanation.surface: A cyborg policeman nabs a little Egyptian man exposing himself in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: RoboCop is the title cyborg of the 1987 film; the 'small' letter is held mid-name, and the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroboscope is an instrument that emits rapid flashes of light, so it is a 'flasher', hence the question mark.

clue.text: Extends gold toilets outside front of mansion

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: one item sits outside another, wrapping around it

parts.note: the gents is a men's public toilet

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of mansion

explanation.surface: A wealthy owner adds gold-fitted lavatories outside the main house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gents' is the British term for a men's public lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: To augment is to increase or enlarge something, which is to extend it.

clue.text: Rudely infers assembly instructions from IKEA may not be this

definitions.text: instructions from IKEA may not be this

indicators.note: an assembly is a putting-together of parts, so the preceding letters are built into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tartly concludes that flat-pack furniture instructions are hard to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assembly instructions' reads as one phrase, but 'assembly' is the anagram signal and the definition starts at 'instructions'.
explanation.definitionFit: User-friendly means easy for ordinary people to use, which baffling IKEA diagrams arguably are not; IKEA is the Swedish flat-pack furniture chain.

clue.text: Broadcast about to contain a cycle event

indicators.note: one item set to contain another wraps around it

parts.note: to relay a programme is to broadcast it
re means concerning, about
taken as written
c is an abbreviation for cycle, as in c/s, cycles per second

explanation.surface: A cycling event is to be televised.
explanation.walkthrough: The A and C go inside RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A relay race is an athletics or swimming event in which team members take turns.

clue.text: For best results, soldiers need this protective layer to be cracked

definitions.text: For best results, soldiers need this protective layer to be cracked

parts.words: For best results, soldiers need this protective layer to be cracked
parts.note: surface reading: troops must break through a defensive line such as armour

parts.words: For best results, soldiers need this protective layer to be cracked
parts.note: setter's reading: soldiers are strips of toast, dipped into a soft-boiled egg once its top is broken

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'soldiers' are fingers of toast for dipping into a boiled egg.
explanation.definitionFit: The thin hard outer covering of an egg protects its contents and must be broken before dipping toast in the yolk.

clue.text: Rebuild oblong cage in old part of Africa

indicators.note: rebuilding puts the parts together in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A zoo instruction to reconstruct a rectangular enclosure in a former African territory.
explanation.definitionFit: The Belgian Congo was Belgium's colony in central Africa until 1960, now the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

clue.text: Fashionable and exclusive scents — initially they're found in Boots!

parts.note: in means in fashion
sole rights are exclusive rights

indicators.note: initially points to the opening character of the next word

parts.note: first letter of scents

explanation.surface: Trendy exclusive perfumes are on sale at Boots, the British high-street chemist.
explanation.walkthrough: Boots is a British chemist chain that sells perfume; the capital B disguises ordinary boots.
explanation.definitionFit: Insoles are inner soles placed inside shoes and footwear for comfort, so they are found in boots.

clue.text: One snaps in the judge's room

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a device that takes snapshots
second meaning: a judge's private chamber

explanation.walkthrough: 'In camera' is the legal phrase for proceedings held in private, from the Latin for chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a photographic apparatus and the Latin for a room, used of a judge's private chambers.

clue.text: What Persians use to view jewels?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Persians are a breed of cat, and they see with their own eyes
second meaning: chatoyant gemstones with a shimmering band of light

explanation.walkthrough: 'Persians' suggests people of Iran; here they are long-haired cats.
explanation.definitionFit: Cat's-eye is the name of a semi-precious gem, often chrysoberyl, whose sheen looks like a cat's pupil.

clue.text: Pig runs in front

indicators.note: one item placed in another goes inside it

parts.note: a pig of a person is a beast
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A pig makes a run for it at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The breast is the front of the body, as in the breast of a bird or a jacket.

clue.text: Nut heading for coffee in Costa, say

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: costa is the anatomical Latin for a rib, which is an example of a bone

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its opening character

parts.note: first letter of coffee

explanation.surface: Heading to Costa, the British coffee-shop chain, for a coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Costa' looks like the coffee chain; it is the Latin for rib, defined by example ('say').
explanation.definitionFit: Bonce and nut are both British slang for the head.

clue.text: Italian city museum enthralling English chap

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so one part holds the others inside

parts.note: the V&A is London's Victoria and Albert Museum
standard abbreviation
a typical man's name

explanation.surface: An Italian city's museum captivates a visiting Englishman.
explanation.definitionFit: Verona is a city in north-east Italy, the setting of Romeo and Juliet.

clue.text: Academic takes solitary type out to see city dweller

indicators.note: taking someone out means they go around you as escort, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: a solitary person is a loner
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A lecturer invites a recluse on an outing to see the sights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes ... out' reads as a date, but the academic ends up inside the solitary type.
explanation.definitionFit: A Londoner is a resident of London, so a dweller in that particular city.

clue.text: Solemn person taking top off dish

indicators.note: removing the top of a down entry strips its opening letter

parts.note: a bowl is a dish

explanation.surface: A serious person lifts the lid off a serving dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Owls look grave and wise, so a solemn, bookish-looking person is called an owl.

clue.text: Stick may break in the middle

parts.note: 'can' and 'may' both express permission

indicators.note: the middle of a five-letter word is its third, central character

parts.note: centre letter of break

explanation.surface: A stick might snap in two at its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A cane is a walking stick or a rod used for support or punishment.

clue.text: Bloomer ruined tree? I'll say!

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked out of its original form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: An exasperated gardener confirms that a tree has indeed been ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a blunder; here it means a plant that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: The Easter lily is a white trumpet-shaped flower, and a flower is a bloomer because it blooms.
